timeline.body:
The cluster coordination consistency layer relies on a couple of fields within `Metadata` which record the last _committed_ values on each node. In contrast, the rest of the cluster state can only be changed at _accept_ time.

In the past we would copy these fields over from the master on every publication, but since #90101 we don't copy anything at all if the `Metadata` is unchanged on the master. However, the master computes the diff against the last _committed_ state whereas the receiving nodes apply the diff to the last _accepted_ state, and this means if the master sends a no-op `Metadata` diff then the receiving node will revert its last-committed values to the ones included in the state it last accepted.

With this commit we include the last-committed values alongside the cluster state diff so that they are always copied properly.

Closes #90158

Alternative to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/92258 that doesn't involve changing the safety algorithm. Not as bad as I thought it would be.

Repeating here: I think this bug is more of a liveness concern than a safety one: it means that an election may incorrectly wait to collect votes from the previous configuration as well as the current one.

~NB no tests yet, I was to see this run through CI first.~ (edit: now has tests)

cc @henningandersen who may have a different opinion about calling this a blocker for 8.6.0.
cc @kingherc who I believe will be doing the 8.6.0 version bump.

timeline.body: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

Feels odd to protect the logging by something we assert on above?

```suggestion
            if (lastAcceptedState.metadata().clusterUUIDCommitted() == false) {
```

reply.body: Ehh I just kept the same logic as before but I don't think I've ever seen this assertion trip. I'd be ok to drop it.

timeline.body: Should we pass in `hasClusterUuid || lastAcceptedState.metadata().clusterUUIDCommitted()` here? I mean, we are outside assertions already, so could also pass in true. But assuming assertions have some case we are trying to protect against, passing in the original committed value seems safer and also in line with original code.
I think the code is cleaner, but I failed to spot the important difference, is it just the logging you wanted out of this?

reply.body: I don't think this does anything different, there's just no need to use a `Metadata.Builder` here any more.
Thanks. In that case, let us revert this and move this to a follow-up, where we can also assume that assertions are held (i.e., use `true` instead of `hasClusterUuid` later in the code).

timeline.body: Left a few comments, probably to be considered questions.
@DaveCTurner should this be 8.6.0 since it's intended to be backported?

reply.body: I'll adjust that while backporting. If I set this to 8.6.0 now then the BwC test suite would fail on this PR, but it's important for those tests to pass because they tell us whether there are any other more subtle BwC problems here.

Joining the dots here:

- I opened a PR at https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/92277 which backports this to 8.6 with a fixed BwC version, and waited for it to pass CI.
- I merged 296eacd1a3b2c41275dddafc3469f60d309d7344 which disables the BwC tests in `main`.
- I merged the backport PR.
- I opened another PR at https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/92280 to fix up the BwC version in `main` and reinstate the BwC tests, which will be merged once it passes CI.

Can we add something like:

```
assertSame(receivedState.nodes(), firstReceivedState.nodes());
```
where `firstReceivedState` is the `receivedState` from the `context0` invocation above? It is mostly a test validation, i.e., that we do send a diff in this case (which AFAICS, we will).

reply.body: Yep, and we can see that from the receiving node's `PublishClusterStateStats` too. See b910c87aaed.
